method: Editorial research plus model support; no fitted blend and no verified betting edge. Daily ordering is editorial, with currently actionable picks placed first.

games.headline: Detroit’s spacing meets Boston’s perimeter offense.
games.analysis: Our working script is a competitive game with Boston leaning on Tatum’s perimeter scoring and Detroit using Cunningham’s creation to find shooters. White’s rebounding is a separate role-based angle. The picks depend on their price, and Detroit winning is a game-script lean rather than a verified moneyline edge.
games.winnerReason: Script lean: Detroit’s ball movement and perimeter finishing hold up at home. Boston’s new lineup and Tatum’s scoring are the main threats.

picks.label: Derrick White · 4+ rebounds
picks.thesis: White’s regular minutes and established rebounding contribution make four boards a reasonable threshold to research. Our minutes sensitivity check remained supportive.
picks.risk: Tatum and Mitchell Robinson compete for the same rebounds. A quieter defensive-rebounding game can leave White short.
evidence: Archived regular-season appearances: 53 of 77 reached four rebounds in 2025–26; 47 of 76 in 2024–25.
Preseason role check: seven rebounds across two appearances totaling 46 minutes. Small sample, not a forecast.

picks.label: Jayson Tatum · 4+ made threes
picks.thesis: Tatum attempted ten and eight threes in his two preseason appearances. The case is built on shot volume, with the price leaving room for an inconsistent shooting night.
picks.risk: Four makes remains a high-variance outcome. His return-season record was weaker than his healthy baseline, and Paul George can absorb shots.
evidence: Preseason: seven makes on 18 attempts in 56 minutes. Do not extrapolate that percentage.
Archived 2024–25: four or more threes in 36 of 72 regular-season games; 2025–26: five of 16.

picks.label: Duncan Robinson · 3+ made threes
picks.thesis: Four preseason starts and 18 three-point attempts in 76 minutes support Robinson’s shooting role alongside Cunningham. Three makes is a role-and-price play.
picks.risk: Detroit has several other wings. In our lower-minutes scenario the apparent price advantage disappeared after fees.
evidence: Preseason: ten makes on 18 attempts. The hot shooting is not assumed to continue.
Archived 2025–26: three or more threes in 46 of 75 valid regular-season appearances.

combo.title: Detroit wins a perimeter scoring battle
combo.script: Detroit wins with Cunningham creating perimeter opportunities and Duncan Robinson making at least three threes. Tatum keeps Boston competitive with at least four threes of his own. This is a plausible shared script, not a claim that every leg is positively correlated.
combo.risk: Boston can win the shooting battle; Robinson can lose minutes; Tatum may attack inside instead. Even a close game can miss both shooting thresholds.

games.headline: New York’s continuity against Philadelphia’s new creators.
games.analysis: The matchup centers on the Brunson–Towns partnership against a reshaped Philadelphia lineup. We prefer researching Towns as a scorer and Maxey as a facilitator, while accounting for James and Brown sharing possession. Preseason workload is context, not a full-game minutes guarantee.
games.winnerReason: Script lean: New York’s established offense creates cleaner late-game possessions. Philadelphia’s talent can easily overturn that continuity advantage.

picks.label: Karl-Anthony Towns · 20+ points
picks.thesis: Towns reached 20 points in 41 of 74 archived regular-season appearances last season. His scoring role alongside Brunson gives this threshold a case at a discounted price.
picks.risk: His preseason shot volume was modest: eight attempts in 29 minutes in the finale. Embiid’s defense and a passing-heavy role could keep him below 20.
evidence: Archived 2025–26: 20.1 points per valid appearance; 20+ in 41 of 74 games.
Preseason finale: 13 points, 15 rebounds and nine assists. That is counterevidence to assuming a scoring surge.

picks.label: Tyrese Maxey · 6+ assists
picks.thesis: Maxey’s historical passing volume supports six assists at a low ask. The new scoring options could improve conversion on his passes if he retains enough ball-handling responsibility.
picks.risk: James and Brown also create offense. Better teammates do not automatically mean more Maxey assists, and his prior workload may fall.
evidence: Archived 2025–26: six or more assists in 47 of 70 valid regular-season appearances; 6.6 assists per game.
The projected starting group contains Maxey, Edgecombe, Brown, James and Embiid; the distribution of touches is uncertain.

picks.label: Jalen Brunson · Under 3.5 rebounds
picks.thesis: Brunson’s offensive responsibilities and New York’s established rebounders make fewer than four boards a plausible angle—but only at a lower price.
picks.risk: His rebounding increased last season. He also collected four and five boards in two preseason games, so this is not a strong recent-trend under.
evidence: Archived 2025–26: fewer than four rebounds in 42 of 73 valid games; 3.37 rebounds per game.
The price ceiling is deliberately below the observed ask at review time. This is a watch candidate until that changes.

combo.title: New York’s offense settles first
combo.script: New York wins with Towns contributing at least 20 points. Philadelphia generates enough offense through Maxey’s passing for six assists, but the new group falls short late. The assist leg can succeed even if scoring is shared across the Sixers.
combo.risk: Towns could facilitate rather than score, or James could dominate Philadelphia’s creation. Neither prop requires a Knicks win; this is a scenario to price, not an assumed correlation advantage.

games.headline: Oklahoma City’s size against San Antonio’s guard-heavy look.
games.analysis: San Antonio’s reported guard-heavy starting group creates a different rebounding matchup for Oklahoma City. Our central angle is Gilgeous-Alexander’s scoring workload; Hartenstein’s boards and Wembanyama’s passing are more sensitive to minutes and defensive choices.
games.winnerReason: Script lean: Oklahoma City gets enough half-court scoring from Gilgeous-Alexander and second possessions from its size. Wembanyama’s defensive impact remains a major threat.

picks.label: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander · 30+ points
picks.thesis: Gilgeous-Alexander’s established scoring workload is more persuasive than a few short preseason appearances. Thirty points fits his normal role if the game stays competitive.
picks.risk: Wembanyama’s rim protection and San Antonio’s perimeter defenders can lower efficiency. Preseason scoring was muted, so a slow start is a real possibility.
evidence: Archived 2025–26: 30+ points in 43 of 68 valid regular-season appearances; 31.1 points per game.
Preseason: 17, 15 and 17 points in 18, 23 and 26 minutes. These were not full regular-season workloads.

picks.label: Isaiah Hartenstein · 10+ rebounds
picks.thesis: Oklahoma City’s size against a reported guard-heavy Spurs group offers a rebounding rationale. Hartenstein’s last full preseason appearance produced eight boards in 19 minutes.
picks.risk: His playing time can shrink against mobile lineups, and Holmgren competes for boards. Last season’s hit rate leaves only a narrow cushion at this price.
evidence: Archived 2025–26: ten or more rebounds in 20 of 47 valid games, compared with 38 of 57 in 2024–25.
Preseason evidence is mixed: one rebound in 13 minutes before the eight-rebound outing.

picks.label: Victor Wembanyama · 4+ assists
picks.thesis: If Oklahoma City sends help toward Wembanyama, San Antonio’s guards give him passing outlets. Four assists is a plausible script leg only at a sufficiently discounted price.
picks.risk: Fox, Castle and Harper can handle most creation themselves. Four assists occurred in only 22 of 63 archived appearances last season.
evidence: Preseason assists across four appearances: one, six, three and two. No consistent six-assist trend is assumed.
The ceiling is below the observed ask. A coherent passing story does not justify paying any price.

combo.title: Shai scores; San Antonio counters through passing
combo.script: Oklahoma City wins behind at least 30 points from Gilgeous-Alexander. San Antonio responds to help defense by moving the ball through Wembanyama for at least four assists. The passing leg remains a price watch, so this combination is not currently ready to price as a value recommendation.
combo.risk: Wembanyama may finish possessions himself, and San Antonio’s guards may supply the assists instead. A Spurs win breaks the script regardless of either player’s production.
